_doc: Security patterns of the SOURCE app, reported on screen 1 ('To fix before any real data': a server-side route named /env first) and in the detail's 'Security' line — they never change the verdict and never block the POC, and are never copied as-is to the target (the plan's changes fix them). Regexes run on committed code files; `absent_in_file`: flag only when the file has no such call; `group_name`: capture group named in the message. env-route (five entries, one per way a framework registers a route) matches the REGISTRATION of a route whose path is literally /env, /debug/env, /api/env, /printenv or /environment: a decorator or annotation, Go HandleFunc/Handle (also a Go 1.22 'GET /env' pattern), ASP.NET MapGet/MapPost, a verb call with the path first and a handler second (an inline function — Express, Fastify, Hono, gin, echo, chi, Slim — a named handler, a Laravel 'Controller@method' string, a list of handlers such as Laravel's [Controller::class, 'method'], or an options object followed by the handler: fastify.get('/env', { schema }, handler)), a Django path(), Flask add_url_rule(). A CLIENT call to such a path (axios, fetch, http.Get, requests.get, this.httpService.get) is not a route and does not match: `skip_client` drops a verb call whose receiver is named like an HTTP client (`client_receiver`: axios*, $, jQuery, http*, *client, *fetch*, request*, got, ky, superagent, MSW's rest…), and a second argument named like a configuration (config, opts, options, params, headers…) is not a handler. `path_group`: the capture group is the route path; scan.sh reports ONE finding per file and id (the first registration, its line), with `path` (its path, with the leading slash) and `paths` (every path of the file, in order): the exact input of a fix that closes a route without touching the code, `clever domain add <fqdn>/<path>` then removing the default domain. Spring and Next.js file-based routes are partly covered (annotations yes, app/env/route.ts no).
